newsitem.title: IRAQ: Talabani rebels in Iraq regain two more towns - UN.
newsitem.headline: Talabani rebels in Iraq regain two more towns - UN.

text.p: Kurdish guerrillas of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) have retaken two more towns from pro-Baghdad rivals of Kurdistan Democratic Party, U.N. officials and guards in Iraqi Kurdistan said on Monday.

PUK rebels led by Jalal Talabani retook Sulaimaniya, Iraqi Kurdistan's biggest city, on Sunday from the KDP and have since regained control of most of the territory they lost to the rival KDP of Massoud Barzani six weeks ago.
The sources said Talabani's guerrillas had now recaptured Degala and Koi Sanjaq after taking control over the strategic Dokan Dam area, site of a major hydroelectirc power project.

"They (PUK rebels) seem to be advancing. They are in Degala and Koi Sanjaq. Fighting is continuing and both sides are using artillery and rocket launchers," one U.N. official told Reuters by telephone from Arbil.
He said it was not yet clear whether Talabani, whose forces were overrun by Baghdad-backed KDP last month, would make any moves towards Arbil, the region's administrative centre.
Talabani said in an interview published on Monday he had no plans to advance on Arbil, which he said was surrounded by Iraqi troops.
Iraqi leaders on Sunday urged both factions to put their differences aside and resume dialogue with Baghdad for a peaceful settlement of the Kurdish issue.

U.N. personnel and guards in Arbil said Iraqi troops were not involved in this round of fighting. Late in August Iraq sent tank-equipped troops into the Kurdish areas to help Barzani oust PUK from Arbil.

Baghdad's move sparked retaliatory missile strikes by the U.S. against targets in southern Iraq. Iraq then said its military interference was in response to a request from Barzani to thwart what it described as an Iranian-backed conspiracy in northern Iraq.
Barzani on Sunday accused Iranian forces of entering northern Iraq to help rivals retake Sulaimaniya and called for international aid against "Iran's brutal invasion".
Iraq on Sunday issued a stern warning to its rebellious Kurds against any dealing with foreign powers.

State-controlled newspapers on Monday splashed their front pages with a statement from the Revolutionary Command Council and leaders of the ruling Baath party calling on Kurds to start peace talks with Baghdad.
